chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the obligatory Zihar. He said: 'That which the man intends by it, exactly.'

key_terms.الظِّهَار: Zihar: A form of divorce in Islamic law where a husband declares his wife to be like his mother's back, making sexual relations with her forbidden until expiation is made.
key_terms.الوَاجِب: The obligatory: Referring to the legal status or requirement associated with the act.
key_terms.بِعَيْن: Exactly / Specifically: Emphasizing that the ruling depends on the precise intention of the individual.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and legal basis for Zihar in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that the legal binding of Zihar is contingent upon the husband's specific intention (niyyah) to use the term as a divorce mechanism, rather than mere utterance. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the principle that verbal declarations require intent to effectuate legal status changes, distinguishing it from general speech. This ruling aligns with the broader Shia emphasis on internal intent as a primary determinant in marital law.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Bin Musa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Zahaar, the obligatory. Heasws said: ‘That which the man intends by it, exactly’.
en.sarwar: 26. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan from “Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Zihar (calling one’s wife as one’s mother) which brings about the obligation.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is exactly that whereby a man wants al- Zihar.’”
